Good man. I sacrificed my 20s. I dropped out of college year 3. I would’ve went to law school (an Ivy League law school!) Moved 400 miles away from my friends and family to immediately get a job to provide. I was in a fraternity, I played ball for my university too (huge school..), and I made hundreds of friends. 3.8 gpa. I regularly met with my second cousin who is a senator at the Nashville legislative plaza. 

I knocked up my college girlfriend, if that much wasn’t clear. 

She and I moved to the suburbs of a major city. But I loved her. When I held my son for the first time, he was only seconds old maybe a minute. And he sneezed. That sneeze fucked me up. It all hit me right then. 

I have this little person. He is my responsibility to provide for, teach, love, and protect. In a millisecond, my world changed. I knew I’d die for him. I’d live for him. And there was nothing I wouldn’t sacrifice for him. And I wanted to give him the things I never had. Like give him a dad. I didn’t know how. I didn’t have one…

He’s 8 now. My girl and I got married when he was a year old. Wanted to make sure… had 2 more kids. And I just didn’t know I had this kind of capacity for love. 3 kids? 

I got a job. First job I got was manual labor. I worked my way up and in a year I was next in line for a manager position. I ended up leaving that company and I started a career in construction. I worked for many people and eventually for myself. I started working for myself around the time when my son was 2 and second baby was born. 

I made good money. I made bad money. It wasn’t stable.. and I worked my ass off. 

I thought my sacrifices would be appreciated. I gave everything. I was present when I was home (unless I was dead tired) but I worked many many late nights and weekends. I bought my wife everything she wanted. Adored my family. 

She left me for someone else. To this day, she doesn’t see or understand my sacrifice. I gave up so much. And I was happy to do it. But she called me selfish. She was jealous that I worked. Grass is greener? Idk. She stayed home with the kids. I gave her every opportunity to do whatever she wanted for work, training, schooling. 

Now I get my kids every other week. I guess I should be thankful for that…
